question: Why did the authors pick sinusoidal positional encodings, and what happened when they tried learned positional embeddings?
final_text: I couldn't find this in the passages I retrieved from the three papers, so I won't guess. I searched: AIAYN §3.5 Positional Encoding; AIAYN §6.2 Model Variations; AIAYN §3.4 Embeddings and Softmax; AIAYN §5.4 Regularization.
drafts: The authors chose sinusoidal positional encodings because they hypothesized that the functions would allow the model to easily learn to attend by relative positions, since for any fixed offset k the encoding at position pos + k can be represented as a linear function of the encoding at position pos, and because the sinusoidal version may allow the model to extrapolate to sequence lengths longer than those encountered during training [AIAYN:3.5:c020]. The authors also experimented with learned positional embeddings and found that the two versions produced nearly identical results, with the learned version yielding a dev perplexity of 4.92 and BLEU of 25.7, matching the base model’s performance [AIAYN:3.5:c020][AIAYN:T3:r08][AIAYN:6.2:c031].

The authors chose the sinusoidal function because they hypothesized it would allow the model to easily learn to attend by relative positions, since for any fixed offset k, PE_pos+k can be represented as a linear function of PE_pos [AIAYN:3.5:c020]. They also chose the sinusoidal version because it may allow the model to extrapolate to sequence lengths longer than the ones encountered during training [AIAYN:3.5:c020]. The authors also experimented with using learned positional embeddings instead, and found that the two versions produced nearly identical results (see Table 3 row (E)) [AIAYN:3.5:c020]. In row (E) the authors replace their sinusoidal positional encoding with learned positional embeddings, and observe nearly identical results to the base model [AIAYN:6.2:c031]. In Table 3, the (E) configuration has PPL / (dev) = 4.92 and BLEU / (dev) = 25.7 [AIAYN:T3:r08].
